structure: Independent positive multiplicative marginal rescaling to historical US arithmetic means; preserve ranks and provisional source relative shapes, leaving historical pairing to the separate analysis.
parameter_provenance: TC 196 mg/dL and HDL 52.5 mg/dL are the supplied 2007–2010 age-standardized US means. Both are transferred as reference-scenario anchors, not as known later-period values.
The realized dimensionless coefficients are 196/mean(input TC) and 52.5/mean(input HDL). Finite-grid normalization avoids quantile-discretization drift in the anchor means.
The shape exponent is fixed at 1 by assumption. Mwanza's smaller admissible single-marker lognormal scales are retained through proportional scaling; no new variance or tail parameter is fitted.

Mwanza adults aged 18+, nonfasting measurements and different geography/case mix do not establish target marginal shape. Shape retention is a transparent working assumption rather than a claim of transportability.
All supplied confidence intervals concern population estimates. None is treated as a person-level standard deviation or used to generate individual variability.
requested_estimands: Primary: after applying historical rank pairings, compute the fraction with TC minus HDL at least 160 mg/dL. This depends on both marginal tails and pairing; it cannot be calculated from these unpaired columns alone.
Mean non-HDL: under equal-weight use of the returned grids, it is 196 minus 52.5 = 143.5 mg/dL, regardless of permutation pairing, up to floating-point error.
Mean individual TC/HDL: calculate only after pairing. The ratio of anchor means, 196/52.5 approximately 3.7333, is not the mean individual ratio. The source individual-ratio mean 3.66 is not imposed.
Single-marker cutoff rates: calculate directly from each transformed marginal using the intended thresholds; source absolute cutoff prevalences are not preserved.
Rank correlation: each biomarker's ranks are unchanged, so Spearman correlation under any fixed historical pairing is unchanged. Side-by-side output rows do not themselves define that pairing.
limitations: No later-period US measurements are supplied, so temporal changes are unidentified. This reference scenario must not be presented as a validated later-surveillance prevalence estimate.
The primary non-HDL tail probability is especially sensitive to unverified marginal dispersion, tail form and pairing. Historical means alone do not identify it.
No target age strata or survey weights are supplied. Anchoring to age-standardized means does not perform direct age standardization of the distributions or identify age-standardized cutoff rates.
The returned grids are equal-weight marginal representations. Subsequent unequal person weights would generally change their means unless handled consistently.
Independent marginal rescaling and subsequent historical pairing do not enforce person-level TC greater than or equal to HDL; no diagnostic or patient-level interpretation is assigned.
Source confidence intervals, historical-mean uncertainty, temporal uncertainty and shape uncertainty are not propagated in this deterministic reference scenario.
